title: Equality and hashing
hook: Equals without GetHashCode is a Dictionary bug waiting for a cache miss. IEquatable<T> avoids boxing. Records generate a consistent pair; hand-rolled DTOs often do not.

sections.heading: Reference equality versus value equality
sections.prose: object.ReferenceEquals and the default class == test identity. Value equality asks whether the data matches. Structs default to field-by-field equality (slow, reflection-ish historically, now more generated but still easy to get wrong with floats and unused fields). Records generate value equality including the runtime type, so a derived record is not equal to a base record with the same properties. Strings are the model citizen: immutable, value-equal, stable hash.

sections.heading: Dictionaries, Redis keys, and IEquatable
sections.prose: Dictionary<TKey, TValue> buckets with GetHashCode then confirms with Equals. The contract: if Equals is true, hashes must match; hashes matching does not imply Equals. Mutating a key after insert orphans the entry. IEquatable<T> gives a typed Equals that does not box T when T is a struct — implement it alongside overrides of Object.Equals and GetHashCode. For Redis cache keys, prefer a readonly record struct or a string you own; do not use a mutable class.

snippets.label: IEquatable cache key used in a dictionary
snippets.explanation: Two different struct copies lookup the same slot because Equals and GetHashCode agree. HashCode.Combine is the .NET helper; keep the fields identical to Equals.

sections.heading: Operators and records
sections.prose: If you overload ==, overload !=, and keep them consistent with Equals (module 04 operators). Records already do this. For classes that stay identity-based, do not overload == or you will confuse every reviewer who writes if (handler == null) versus if (handler is null) — the latter still uses a different pattern in modern C#. EqualityComparer<T>.Default is what collections use; custom comparers belong at the dictionary constructor, not hidden inside GetHashCode with randomness.

interviewTakeaways: Equals and GetHashCode are a pair; collections depend on it.
IEquatable<T> avoids boxing for value types.
Never mutate a dictionary key; records help only if they stay immutable.
commonPitfalls: Overriding Equals on a class but leaving the default reference GetHashCode.
Using a mutable DTO as a HashSet element across a high-concurrency submit path.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS objects compare by reference; there is no IEquatable. Map keys use SameValueZero. C# dictionaries use the type’s equality contract.
TS cannot generate Equals/GetHashCode. You write your own or use a library. C# records generate both.
